questions.question: What must be true before two runs can be merged by repeatedly taking the smaller front value?
questions.explanation: The front value is known to be the smallest remaining value only inside a sorted run.
optionFeedback: Runs of different lengths merge correctly.
Correct: sorted runs are the merge helper's precondition.
They are normally ranges or temporary arrays in one program.

questions.question: Why must leftover values be copied after one run becomes empty?
options: They are already sorted but have not yet entered the result
They need to be compared with zero
They are duplicates that must be deleted
questions.explanation: Every value in the nonempty run is larger than or equal to the values already chosen, so it can be copied directly.
optionFeedback: Correct: no more cross-run comparison is needed, but the values still belong in the output.
The merge helper does not restart recursion.

questions.question: Why is merge sort O(n log n)?
options: There are log n levels and O(n) merge work per level
It has two loops, so their costs multiply
Every value is compared with every other value
questions.explanation: Repeated halving creates logarithmically many levels, and each level processes all n values across its merges.
optionFeedback: Correct: n work across each of log n levels.
Loop nesting alone is not the derivation here.
A merge over n values is linear, not constant.

questions.question: What is the base case for mergeSort(arr, start, end)?
questions.explanation: A range with zero or one element is already sorted, so recursion stops when start >= end.
optionFeedback: Correct: this covers empty and one-element ranges.
The final valid end index is arr.length - 1.
That expression does not describe range size.
